ECIV 101.description: Fundamental concepts in each of the disciplines of civil engineering are discussed. Critical thinking skills are formally fostered by hands-on experiences and group discussions.
ECIV 101.subject: ECIV
ECIV 101.title: Introduction to Civil Engineering

ECIV 111.description: Principles and practice of visualization and graphical representation using modern computer-aided design tools.
ECIV 111.subject: ECIV
ECIV 111.title: Introduction to Engineering Graphics and Visualization

ECIV 200.description: Fundamentals of engineering mechanics. Equilibrium of particles and rigid bodies. Free-body diagrams, analysis trusses and frames. Distributed forces, centroids, centers of gravity, and friction.
ECIV 200.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 141.
ECIV 200.subject: ECIV
ECIV 200.title: Statics

ECIV 201.description: The use of computational tools and techniques for solving civil and environmental engineering problems. Overview of numerical methods including roots of equations, systems of linear equations, interpolation, and integration. Analysis of civil and environmental systems.
ECIV 201.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 142 and ECIV 200 or ENCP 200.
ECIV 201.subject: ECIV
ECIV 201.title: Computational Methods for Civil Engineering

ECIV 210.description: Kinematics of particles and rigid bodies. Vector representation of force and motion. Free-body diagrams, application of energy and momentum methods to solve problems. Rigid body and central force motion.
ECIV 210.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECIV 200 or ENCP 200; C or better in MATH 142.
ECIV 210.subject: ECIV
ECIV 210.title: Dynamics

ECIV 220.description: Concepts of stress and strain; stress analysis of basic structural members. Vectors, free bodies, equilibrium and elastic behavior. Combined stress, Mohr’s circle. Beams, columns, torsion, and rotation.
ECIV 220.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECIV 200 or ENCP 200 and in MATH 142.
ECIV 220.subject: ECIV
ECIV 220.title: Mechanics of Solids

ECIV 230.description: Broad exposure to how construction projects are planned and executed including the use of construction equipment, site planning, quality control, and construction safety.
ECIV 230.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 101 and C or better in MATH 141.
ECIV 230.subject: ECIV
ECIV 230.title: Introduction to Construction Engineering

ECIV 270.description: Introduces students to civil engineering design through projects that address community needs.
ECIV 270.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 141.
ECIV 270.subject: ECIV
ECIV 270.title: Fundamentals of Civil Engineering Design

ECIV 300.description: Theory and application of plane surveying and mapping techniques. Lecture plus laboratory.
ECIV 300.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in MATH 241.
ECIV 300.subject: ECIV
ECIV 300.title: Civil Engineering Measurements

ECIV 303.description: Mechanical and thermal properties of mineral aggregates, cements, concrete, timber, asphalt, metals, and plastics.
ECIV 303.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECIV 220 or ENCP 260.
ECIV 303.subject: ECIV
ECIV 303.title: Civil Engineering Materials

ECIV 303L.description: Experiments, exercises, and demonstrations to accompany ECIV 303 .
ECIV 303L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in STAT 509 or STAT 511.
ECIV 303L.subject: ECIV
ECIV 303L.title: Civil Engineering Materials Laboratory

ECIV 307.description: Regulatory permits and scheduling of construction projects. Engineering responsibility and liabilities. Reporting of engineering designs and analysis. Cost estimation of engineering projects including present or future net value.
ECIV 307.subject: ECIV
ECIV 307.title: Professional Development for Civil Engineers

ECIV 320.description: Equilibrium, shear and moment diagrams, and influence lines for statically determinate trusses, beams, and frames. Energy principles and other methods for displacement calculations. Introduction to indeterminate structural analysis.
ECIV 320.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in MATH 242; C or better in ECIV 220 or ENCP 260.
ECIV 320.subject: ECIV
ECIV 320.title: Structural Analysis I

ECIV 325.description: Behavior and design of steel beams, columns, and tension members; strength and stability; design of connections using welded, bolted and riveted construction.
ECIV 325.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECIV 320.
ECIV 325.subject: ECIV
ECIV 325.title: Structural Steel Design

ECIV 327.description: Behavior and design of reinforced concrete beams, columns, continuous beams and one way slabs, and footings.
ECIV 327.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECIV 320.
ECIV 327.subject: ECIV
ECIV 327.title: Reinforced Concrete Design

ECIV 330.description: Engineering properties of soil and rock; hydraulic conductivity, flow nets, drainage design; consolidation theory, shearing strength of soil.
ECIV 330.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in either ECIV 220 or ENCP 260.
ECIV 330.subject: ECIV
ECIV 330.title: Introduction to Geotechnical Engineering

ECIV 330L.description: Laboratory associated with ECIV 330 . Soil mechanics experiments, exercises, and demonstrations. Three contact hours per week.
ECIV 330L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in STAT 509 or STAT 511.
ECIV 330L.subject: ECIV
ECIV 330L.title: Geotechnical Laboratory

ECIV 340.description: Transportation design, planning, and operational analysis, including roadway, airway, and railway systems; transportation elements, including traveled way, vehicle, control, terminals, and advanced technology; traffic data collection, interpretation, and analysis.
ECIV 340.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 201, ENCP 201, or ECIV 270; D or better in STAT 509 or STAT 511.
ECIV 340.subject: ECIV
ECIV 340.title: Introduction to Transportation Engineering

ECIV 340L.description: Principles of distances, elevations and angles that pertain to roadways, basic theories in engineering measurements and surveying calculations, and an introduction to mapping, for transportation engineering applications. Three contact hours per week.
ECIV 340L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in STAT 509 or STAT 511.
ECIV 340L.subject: ECIV
ECIV 340L.title: Transportation Engineering Laboratory

ECIV 350.description: Concepts of environmental engineering, including air and water pollution, solid and hazardous waste disposal, and noise pollution. Qualitative and quantitative development of engineering techniques for pollution control.
ECIV 350.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CHEM 111 or CHEM 141; C or better in Math 142
ECIV 350.subject: ECIV
ECIV 350.title: Introduction to Environmental Engineering

ECIV 350L.description: Physical, chemical, and biological analysis of water and wastewater. Three laboratory hours per week.
ECIV 350L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in STAT 509 or STAT 511.
ECIV 350L.subject: ECIV
ECIV 350L.title: Introduction to Environmental Engineering Laboratory

ECIV 360.description: Principles of fluid statics and dynamics. Conservation of mass, momentum, and energy. Similitude and dimensional analysis, open channel flow, lift and drag forces, and introduction to turbulent flow.
ECIV 360.subject: ECIV
ECIV 360.title: Fluid Mechanics

ECIV 362.description: Application of fluid mechanic principles to water resources engineering problems; pipe systems, pumps, open channel flow, peak runoff, seepage, hydraulic structures.
ECIV 362.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in either ECIV 360 or ENCP 360.
ECIV 362.subject: ECIV
ECIV 362.title: Introduction to Water Resources Engineering

ECIV 362L.description: Experiments, exercises, and demonstrations on flow in pipes and open channels, pumps, flow measurement, seepage, and infiltration. Three contact hours per week.
ECIV 362L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in STAT 509 or 511.
ECIV 362L.subject: ECIV
ECIV 362L.title: Introduction to Water Resources Engineering Laboratory

ECIV 405.description: Systems approach to analysis and design; application of engineering economic principles to the evaluation of design alternatives; deterministic modeling and optimization emphasizing civil engineering applications.
ECIV 405.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 142.
ECIV 405.subject: ECIV
ECIV 405.title: System Applications in Civil Engineering

ECIV 426.description: Design of steel structures including elastic and plastic design concepts. Design of concrete structures including continuous members and long columns.
ECIV 426.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 325 or ECIV 327.
ECIV 426.subject: ECIV
ECIV 426.title: Structural Design

ECIV 470.description: Application of hydraulic, geotechnical, and structural principles in design; project scheduling; cost estimation; ethics; environmental and social impact; design drawings; report documents.
ECIV 470.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 270 and ECIV 307; D or better in two ECIV Distribution Courses.
ECIV 470.subject: ECIV
ECIV 470.title: Civil Engineering Design

ECIV 490.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by course title. May be repeated as topic varies. A maximum of twelve credits may be applied towards a degree.
ECIV 490.subject: ECIV
ECIV 490.title: Special Topics

ECIV 497.description: Preparation for the Fundamentals of Engineering Exam. Will cover general engineering and civil engineering specific areas. Restricted to Civil Engineering Seniors. Pass/ Fail Grading.
ECIV 497.subject: ECIV
ECIV 497.title: Fundamentals of Engineering Preparation

ECIV 499.description: Individual investigation or studies of special topics. A maximum of six credits may be applied toward a degree.
ECIV 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: approval of project proposal by instructor; USC/GPA 2.8.
ECIV 499.subject: ECIV
ECIV 499.title: Independent Study in Civil and Environmental Engineering

ECIV 502.description: The steps of conducting and interpreting an environmental life cycle assessment of engineered systems. Fundamentals associated with conducting a life cycle assessment, including goal and scope, inventory analysis, impact assessment and interpretation.
ECIV 502.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 350.
ECIV 502.subject: ECIV
ECIV 502.title: Life Cycle Assessment of Engineered Systems

ECIV 503.description: Introduction of structural modeling; strain gauge instrumentation; force, displacement, acceleration, pressure, temperature measurements; concrete and steel modeling; size effects; analysis of experimental data.
ECIV 503.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 327.
ECIV 503.subject: ECIV
ECIV 503.title: Structural Modeling and Experimental Methods

ECIV 520.description: Advanced methods of structural analysis with emphasis on matrix methods. Development of the generalized matrix force and matrix displacement methods of static analysis, with applications to trusses and frames.
ECIV 520.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 320.
ECIV 520.subject: ECIV
ECIV 520.title: Structural Analysis II

ECIV 521.description: Numerical modeling of typical engineering problems. Numerical solution of linear and nonlinear, boundary and initial value problems. Introduction to optimization.
ECIV 521.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 242, or departmental approval.
ECIV 521.subject: ECIV
ECIV 521.title: Numerical Methods in Mechanics

ECIV 524.description: Response of single- and multiple-degree of freedom structurally dynamic systems to impact, harmonic, wind, and seismic excitations.
ECIV 524.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 320.
ECIV 524.subject: ECIV
ECIV 524.title: Structural Vibrations

ECIV 526.description: Basic engineering properties of timber and masonry materials, design methods and philosophies for timber and masonry structures. Particular attention is paid to current codes, specifications and analysis.
ECIV 526.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECIV 320.
ECIV 526.subject: ECIV
ECIV 526.title: Timber and Masonry Design

ECIV 530.description: Subsurface investigation procedures. Theoretical and practical aspects of shallow and deep foundation design.
ECIV 530.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 330 or equivalent.
ECIV 530.subject: ECIV
ECIV 530.title: Foundation Analysis and Design

ECIV 531.description: Geotechnical engineering problems associated with the behavior of earth masses. Soil shear strength, lateral earth pressure, design of retaining structures, slope stability, water flow through soils.
ECIV 531.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 330.
ECIV 531.subject: ECIV
ECIV 531.title: Design of Earth Structures

ECIV 533.description: Principles for the design, construction, and performance of waste containment systems. Characterization of barrier materials; geosynthetics; design of liner and leachate collection systems; stability and deformation analyses of landfills.
ECIV 533.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 330.
ECIV 533.subject: ECIV
ECIV 533.title: Geosynthetics and Geotechnical Design of Landfills

ECIV 535.description: Design and analysis of flexible and rigid pavements. Pavement distress evaluation, subgrade and base course behavior, stress analysis, traffic prediction.
ECIV 535.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 330.
ECIV 535.subject: ECIV
ECIV 535.title: Pavement Analysis and Design

ECIV 539.description: Overview of transducers, signal conditioning and data acquisition; test control methods, data analysis and measurement errors; testing systems to measure soil strength, stiffness, and hydraulic conductivity; laboratory projects and examinations.
ECIV 539.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 330, D or better in ECIV 330L.
ECIV 539.subject: ECIV
ECIV 539.title: Experimental Methods in Geotechnical Engineering

ECIV 540.description: Fundamental interactions between supply and demand in transportation systems. Modeling transportation demand and trip-making behavior. Evaluation of alternatives for decision making.
ECIV 540.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 340.
ECIV 540.subject: ECIV
ECIV 540.title: Transportation Systems Planning

ECIV 541.description: Design of transportation facilities using relevant tools and guidelines with emphasis on physical and operational aspects of arterials, freeways, intersections, and interchanges, including geometry, capacity, control, and safety.
ECIV 541.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 111 or ENCP 102 and D or better in ECIV 340.
ECIV 541.subject: ECIV
ECIV 541.title: Highway Design

ECIV 542.description: Capacity analysis of freeways and arterials. Traffic flow characteristics and basic relationships among traffic flow parameters. Signalized and unsignalized intersection control and signal timing design.
ECIV 542.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 340.
ECIV 542.subject: ECIV
ECIV 542.title: Traffic Engineering

ECIV 543.description: Research concepts and methodologies to enable students to identify the underlying reasons and factors that contribute to traffic crashes and determine appropriate countermeasures.
ECIV 543.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 340.
ECIV 543.subject: ECIV
ECIV 543.title: Traffic Safety Analysis

ECIV 551.description: Unit operations and processes employed in the physical, chemical, and biological treatment of water and wastewater. Design of water and wastewater treatment systems.
ECIV 551.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 350.
ECIV 551.subject: ECIV
ECIV 551.title: Elements of Water and Wastewater Treatment

ECIV 555.description: Fundamentals and engineering principles of solid waste generation, characterization, collection and transport, source reduction and recycling, and physical, chemical, and biological treatment strategies.
ECIV 555.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 350.
ECIV 555.subject: ECIV
ECIV 555.title: Principles of Municipal Solid Waste Engineering

ECIV 556.description: Introduction to the sources of air pollution and the engineering principles used for control and prevention.
ECIV 556.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 350.
ECIV 556.subject: ECIV
ECIV 556.title: Air Pollution Control Engineering

ECIV 557.description: Instruction to sustainable engineering design alternatives and principles for construction and site development from preconstruction through design and the construction phase.
ECIV 557.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 350 and ECIV 570.
ECIV 557.subject: ECIV
ECIV 557.title: Sustainable Construction for Engineers

ECIV 558.description: Modeling fate and transport phenomena in environmental processes with applications in engineered unit operators and natural systems.
ECIV 558.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better ECIV 350 and MATH 242.
ECIV 558.subject: ECIV
ECIV 558.title: Environmental Engineering Process Modeling

ECIV 560.description: Steady and unsteady flows in single or multiple-channel systems.
ECIV 560.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 360 or ENCP 360.
ECIV 560.subject: ECIV
ECIV 560.title: Open Channel Hydraulics

ECIV 562.description: Applications of hydrologic techniques to design problems; stormwater simulation models; urban stormwater.
ECIV 562.subject: ECIV
ECIV 562.title: Engineering Hydrology

ECIV 563.description: Hydrologic cycle, subsurface physical properties, equations of groundwater flow, well flow, well design, groundwater resource development, design of dewatering systems, groundwater contamination.
ECIV 563.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 362 or departmental approval.
ECIV 563.subject: ECIV
ECIV 563.title: Subsurface Hydrology

ECIV 570.description: Fundamentals of designing and permitting the conversion of land to new or altered states, including environmental issues, traffic and parking, utility resources, site engineering, ADA, safety, planning, and zoning requirements.
ECIV 570.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in, Three from ECIV 320, ECIV 330, ECIV 340, ECIV 350, and ECIV 362.
ECIV 570.subject: ECIV
ECIV 570.title: Land Development for Engineers

ECIV 580.description: Introduction to the analysis and design of the railway infrastructure for freight and passenger systems to include track and track support systems, grade crossings, special trackwork, construction, inspection, assessment and compliance.
ECIV 580.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 320, ECIV 330, and ECIV 340.
ECIV 580.subject: ECIV
ECIV 580.title: Railway Engineering I

ECIV 582.description: Principles of rail operations; Network management; Best practices for train planning, performance management and delivery of service; technical elements of a railway from an operations perspective (train controls, signaling, communications, yards, tractive power etc).
ECIV 582.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 340.
ECIV 582.subject: ECIV
ECIV 582.title: Operation and Logistics of Railway Systems

ECIV 588.description: Introduction to railway infrastructure; Structural design considerations and criteria of railway structures; Bridge types and components; Planning and preliminary design of modern railway bridges; Loads and forces; Structural analysis and design of steel railway bridges and components.
ECIV 588.subject: ECIV
ECIV 588.title: Design of Railway Bridges and Structures

ECIV 590.description: The content of this course varies, and the topics are selected by the faculty. The aim of this course is to expose upper-level undergraduate students and graduate students to a contemporary issue, not covered in any Civil and Environmental Engineering course. Possible topics include intelligent infrastructure, sustainable construction, and monitoring and improvement of poor and degrading infrastructure.
ECIV 590.subject: ECIV
ECIV 590.title: Intermediate Special Topics

ECIV 705.description: Planning, design, and operation of large-scale, integrated civil and environmental engineering systems, with applications of mathematical programming and other search models.
ECIV 705.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 405.
ECIV 705.subject: ECIV
ECIV 705.title: Deterministic Civil and Environmental Systems Engineering

ECIV 706.description: Civil and environmental systems engineering under uncertainty, including decision rules, decision theory, uncertainty propagation, stochastic programming, and conservative design.
ECIV 706.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in STAT 509.
ECIV 706.subject: ECIV
ECIV 706.title: Probabilistic Civil and Environmental Systems Engineering

ECIV 707.description: This course focuses in studying the life-cycle of a project using a systems engineering approach. Industry standards for engineering companies as well as practical considerations are studies through the semester.
ECIV 707.subject: ECIV
ECIV 707.title: Management of Engineering Projects

ECIV 708.description: Risk analysis is presented in the context of reliability in design including applications to mechanical and electrical systems with discussion of failure modes and life cycle costs.
ECIV 708.subject: ECIV
ECIV 708.title: Risk Analysis for Engineering Applications

ECIV 712.description: Introduction to boundary element methods and their computer implementation. Steady-state and transient solutions of two- and three-dimensional problems of elasticity and potential flow.
ECIV 712.subject: ECIV
ECIV 712.title: Boundary Element Methods in Engineering

ECIV 720.description: Development of concepts and practical applications of the finite element method of structural analysis with emphasis on the displacement method approach. Initial strains, specified displacements, numerical integration, and isoparametric elements are included.
ECIV 720.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 520.
ECIV 720.subject: ECIV
ECIV 720.title: Advanced Structural Mechanics and Analysis

ECIV 722.description: Development of the fundamental differential equations for plates. Miscellaneous classic plate solutions. Membrane and bending solutions for shells of revolution, circular cylindrical shells, hyperbolic paraboloid shells and circular cylindrical barrel shells.
ECIV 722.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in MATH 242.
ECIV 722.subject: ECIV
ECIV 722.title: Theory and Design of Plates and Shells

ECIV 724.description: Lumped and continuous multidegree of freedom mechanical systems and structural assemblies. Steady-state, shock, and random excitation. Modal analysis, numerical methods. Introduction to wave propagation, earthquake engineering, and nonlinear vibrations.
ECIV 724.subject: ECIV
ECIV 724.title: Dynamics of Structures

ECIV 725.description: Analysis and behavior of metal structural components under general loading combinations. Buckling phenomena of thin-walled open sections in the elastic and inelastic regions, and correlation with design code criteria. Behavior and design of plate girders.
ECIV 725.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 325.
ECIV 725.subject: ECIV
ECIV 725.title: Advanced Analysis and Design in Structural Metals

ECIV 726.description: Analysis and modeling existing and repaired structures. Selection, modeling, and design of repair and/or retrofit measures.
ECIV 726.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 520.
ECIV 726.subject: ECIV
ECIV 726.title: Repair and Retrofit of Structures

ECIV 727.description: Design of multistory structures, two-way slabs, joints in buildings, pavement design, and miscellaneous topics.
ECIV 727.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 327.
ECIV 727.subject: ECIV
ECIV 727.title: Advanced Analysis and Design of Reinforced Concrete

ECIV 728.description: Pre-stressing methods and materials; flexural analysis, shear and torsion, design of simple, composite and continuous beams. Deflections, slab design, and study of axially loaded members.
ECIV 728.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 327.
ECIV 728.subject: ECIV
ECIV 728.title: Prestressed Concrete Analysis and Design

ECIV 730.description: Course covers the mechanical properties of soil; analysis of the field and laboratory tests to determine soil properties required for foundation analysis and design; consolidation theory; and settlement analysis.
ECIV 730.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 530.
ECIV 730.subject: ECIV
ECIV 730.title: Advanced Soil Mechanics

ECIV 731.description: Shear strength of soil and rock under effective stress. Slope stability analysis, tieback and reinforced earth systems. Computation of earth pressures for excavations and tunnels. Dewatering for construction.
ECIV 731.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 530.
ECIV 731.subject: ECIV
ECIV 731.title: Slope Stabilty, Retaining Systems and Lateral Earth Pressure

ECIV 732.description: Constitutive models and their numerical implementation. Elastic and plastic approaches to analysis. Finite element applications to geomechanics problems. Layer analysis, arching, and stability case studies.
ECIV 732.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 530.
ECIV 732.subject: ECIV
ECIV 732.title: Theoretical and Numerical Methods in Geomechanics

ECIV 733.description: Soil mineralogy, chemistry, and clay-water systems. Impact of soil fabric and microstructure on engineering behavior. Soil-contaminant interaction. Barriers and liners for containment.
ECIV 733.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 530.
ECIV 733.subject: ECIV
ECIV 733.title: Physico-chemical Properties of Soils

ECIV 734.description: Properties and behaviors of soils under cyclic and dynamic loading. Seismic hazard assessment. Dynamic response analysis. Soil liquefaction.
ECIV 734.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 530 or ECIV 531.
ECIV 734.subject: ECIV
ECIV 734.title: Soil Dynamics and Geotechnical Earthquake Engineering

ECIV 736.description: Application of soil mechanics principles to improving the engineering characteristics of soil and rock. Topics include mechanisms of soil densification, preconsolidation, grouting, ground freezing, reinforced earth, and soil nailing.
ECIV 736.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 530.
ECIV 736.subject: ECIV
ECIV 736.title: Ground Improvement Techniques

ECIV 737.description: Application of soil mechanics to design and analysis of foundations. Shallow foundations, bearing capacity, settlement. Deep foundations, axial and lateral loading, wave equation analysis, drilled shafts. Design and construction issues.
ECIV 737.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 530.
ECIV 737.subject: ECIV
ECIV 737.title: Advanced Foundation Design

ECIV 742.description: Marine container terminal design and operations, rail-yard design and operations, cross-dock terminal design and operations, drayage routing and scheduling, and network design. Application of operations research techniques to intermodal transportation.
ECIV 742.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 705.
ECIV 742.subject: ECIV
ECIV 742.title: Intermodal Freight Transport

ECIV 744.description: Individual choice theory; binary choice models; unordered multinomial and multi-dimensional choice models; sampling theory and sample design; ordered multinomial models, aggregate prediction with choice models; joint stated preference and revealed preference modeling, and longitudinal choice analysis; review of state-of-the-art and future directions.
ECIV 744.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in STAT 509.
ECIV 744.subject: ECIV
ECIV 744.title: Discrete Choice Analysis of Travel Demand

ECIV 746.description: Design, operation, and management of traffic flows over complex transportation networks. Covers two major topics: traffic flow modeling and traffic flow operations. Includes deterministic and probabilistic models, elements of queueing theory, and traffic assignment. Concepts and methods are illustrated through various applications and examples.
ECIV 746.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 706.
ECIV 746.subject: ECIV
ECIV 746.title: Flows in Transportation Networks

ECIV 748.description: Survey of statistical techniques useful in traffic engineering. Deterministic and stochastic models of traffic flow. Operations research techniques. Simulation by digital computer. Applications to highway problems.
ECIV 748.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 541, D or better in STAT 509.
ECIV 748.subject: ECIV
ECIV 748.title: Traffic Flow Theory

ECIV 750.description: Basic physical, chemical, and biological processes applied to aqueous systems.
ECIV 750.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CHEM 112, C or better in MATH 142.
ECIV 750.subject: ECIV
ECIV 750.title: Principles of Environmental Engineering Process

ECIV 751.description: Physical and chemical water and wastewater treatment processes. Topics include mixing, coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, oxidation, absorption, and ion exchange.
ECIV 751.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 750.
ECIV 751.subject: ECIV
ECIV 751.title: Water and Wastewater Treatment Theory I

ECIV 752.description: Biological water and wastewater treatment process. Topics include activated sludge, biofilms, nutrient removal, lagoons, and sludge treatment and disposal.
ECIV 752.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 750.
ECIV 752.subject: ECIV
ECIV 752.title: Water and Wastewater Treatment Theory II

ECIV 753.description: Laboratory experiments in selected processes for water and wastewater treatment.
ECIV 753.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 350L.
ECIV 753.subject: ECIV
ECIV 753.title: Unit Operations Laboratory for Water and Wastewater Treatment

ECIV 755.description: Industrial sources, characteristics, and treatment plant design.
ECIV 755.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 751 or ECIV 752.
ECIV 755.subject: ECIV
ECIV 755.title: Industrial Wastewater Treatment

ECIV 760.description: Unsteady flow in open channels and pipes: theory, governing equations, and methods for their solution.
ECIV 760.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 560.
ECIV 760.subject: ECIV
ECIV 760.title: Computational Hydraulics

ECIV 761.description: Formation of groundwater flow and solute transport problems, theory and practice, numerical methods, solution techniques.
ECIV 761.subject: ECIV
ECIV 761.title: Numerical Methods in Subsurface Hydrology

ECIV 762.description: Advanced theories and techniques used in stormwater modeling; kinematic hydrology; soil physics infiltration; deterministic and parametric stormwater models; stochastic methods.
ECIV 762.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 562.
ECIV 762.subject: ECIV
ECIV 762.title: Advanced Hydrology

ECIV 763.description: Moisture content-matric suction relationships, theory of flow in unsaturated soils, governing equations, measurement techniques, computer modeling of flow and transport.
ECIV 763.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 563.
ECIV 763.subject: ECIV
ECIV 763.title: Unsaturated Flow Theory

ECIV 764.description: Quantitative study of conservative and non-conservative pollutant transport in groundwater. Special topics include: transport processes, field techniques to determine aquifer transport parameters, and computer modeling of flow and transport.
ECIV 764.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 563.
ECIV 764.subject: ECIV
ECIV 764.title: Contaminant Transport

ECIV 765.description: Erosion, sediment transport, methods for control, pond hydraulics and performance, nonpoint source pollution, stream water quality.
ECIV 765.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ECIV 562.
ECIV 765.subject: ECIV
ECIV 765.title: Erosion and Sediment Control

ECIV 766.description: Definitions; derivation of governing equations; methods of solution; method of characteristics; transients caused by turbomachinery, and methods for controlling transients.
ECIV 766.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in ENCP 360.
ECIV 766.subject: ECIV
ECIV 766.title: Fluid Transients
